where: install.sh, claude section; AD installer contract
silent_on: every claude-* box off: no --include, so AdaptiveDesign falls back to ~/.config/adaptive-design/includes and the boxes no longer decide
chose: Pass nothing and accept the fallback; the contract has no way to say 'none'. A machine with that file and all boxes off gets the file's includes. Worth an explicit '--include none' or similar in AD's contract.

silent_on: how install mode reports a missing clone or a failing AdaptiveDesign install.sh; ok/bad/fix were doctor-only
chose: Use bad and fix in install mode too. Clone missing (or git clone failing) and AD's install.sh exiting non-zero are each one bad line with a fix; the run carries on and exits 0 like other features.

silent_on: AD --check's indented claude-config-check lines, its summary line, the github-mcp check, and the doctor's behaviour with no clone
chose: AD's ok/bad lines and its claude-config-check level<TAB>msg<TAB>hint lines go through ok/warn/bad/fix; headers and the summary are dropped. github-mcp check kept. No clone: one bad line with a fix, no clone attempt (the doctor changes nothing).

silent_on: how to call AdaptiveDesign's install.ps1, whose flags are -Include <name[]> (AD gap M5), not --include
chose: In-process call, & $AdDir\install.ps1 -Include <names>, so it runs under this process's execution policy; no -Include when every claude-* box is off (same fallback as M1). Its exit code ($LASTEXITCODE, reset first) or a thrown error is one bad line with a fix.

silent_on: install.ps1 has no doctor mode and no ok/bad helpers, so there is no check to delegate and no format for a failure
chose: No doctor added (out of scope). A missing clone, failed clone or failed AD install is printed as '  bad  <msg>' in red and '      fix: <hint>', install.sh's format; the run carries on, as M1 does.

silent_on: git may be absent on Windows, and PS 5.1 with $ErrorActionPreference Stop throws on git's stderr if it is redirected
chose: Clone only when git is on PATH and CONFIGME_NO_CLONE is unset; git's stderr is not redirected; success is judged by $LASTEXITCODE. No git: the missing-clone bad line names git as the fix.

silent_on: whether --include core also goes to the --doctor run of AD's install.sh --check, and its order among the boxes
chose: claude_includes prints --include core first, then the boxes in features.md order; both the install and the doctor use it, so --check sees the same set. install.ps1 puts 'core' first in -Include, then the boxes sorted.
